title: Platform systems & services: Playbook, Runbooks, Dashboards, Roadmap, and Team Wiki
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Overview:
This document is the canonical platform engineering playbook for Redwood Inference systems and services. It combines: an inventory of critical services, standardized runbooks for the most common incidents, dashboard and alerting guidance, how-to procedures for oncall and owners, retrospective takeaways, and the next 6–12 month roadmap.

Audience:
- Platform engineers
- SREs and oncall engineers
- Service owners who run inference-related components
- Product/engineering partners responsible for SLAs and rollouts

Scope:
This page covers production-facing platform systems (API gateway, routing, serving runtime, GPU pools, autoscaler, KV/prefix cache services, observability pipeline). Private deployments and customer-specific playbooks are referenced but handled in customer-specific pages.

1) Service inventory (critical systems)
| Service | Primary owner | SLA / SLO | Pager |
|---|---|---:|---|
| api-gateway | platform-api | 99.9% availability, p95 < 80ms | oncall-api |
| routing-proxy | platform-routing | 99.95% availability, failover < 30s | oncall-routing |
| serving-runtime | runtime-team | 99.9% availability, tail latency p99 < 700ms | oncall-runtime |
| gpu-pool-manager | infra-gpu | 99.9% pod availability, scheduling latency < 2m | oncall-gpu |
| kv-prefix-cache | cache-team | eventual consistency, cache hit target 85% | oncall-cache |
| telemetry-pipeline | observability | 99% ingestion availability, 6h retention for traces by default | oncall-obs |

2) Dashboards & alerts (what to monitor)
Core dashboards (owners must maintain these views):
- Platform Overview dashboard (ops/platform): requests per second, error rate, latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), active model variants, GPU utilization by pool.
- Serving Runtime Health (runtime-team): KV cache hit rate, KV tail latencies, model load errors, sequence length distribution heatmap.
- GPU Fleet and Capacity (infra-gpu): node-level GPU memory, GPU utilization per-job, eviction rate, pending scheduling queue.
- API Gateway & Quotas (platform-api): auth failure rate, rate-limit rejections, per-tenant throttles.
- Observability pipeline (observability): ingestion lag, retention failures, sample rates.

Standard alert thresholds (examples — owners may tighten per-service):
- P50 latency increase > 2x for 5m -> Severity P2 alert to owner
- P99 latency > 2s sustained for 2m -> Severity P1, page oncall
- Error rate > 3% of requests for 5m -> Severity P1, page oncall and create incident ticket
- GPU eviction rate > 0.5% in 10m -> page infra-gpu
- KV cache hit < 70% for 10m -> notify cache-team (P2)
- Telemetry ingestion lag > 10m -> notify observability (P2)

Alert routing policy: alerts route to team oncall by default. If alert is during a major incident window (multi-team incident), escalation goes to the Incident Commander (IC) on the platform-sre roster. Pager duty playbook: page primary -> 5 min -> escalate to secondary -> 10 min -> notify IC and eng leadership.

3) Incident runbooks (canonical; keep short and actionable)
- Runbook: API Gateway high error rate (HTTP 5xx)
  1. Detect: alert triggers "api-gateway 5xx rate > 3%". Confirm errors via Platform Overview dashboard and logs.
  2. Impact: customers experience failed requests; potential downstream backpressure. Immediately set incident severity to P1 if customer impact noted.
  3. Mitigation steps:
     a. Check gateway pods: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=api-gateway; review pod restarts and OOMs.
     b. If deployment just rolled: rollback to previous stable revision (kubectl rollout undo).
     c. If upstream dependency failing (auth, routing): temporarily switch to degraded route: toggle feature-flag gateway_fallback=true in the config-service.
     d. If rate spike due to abusive client: cutoff by adding client id to blocklist via admin API.
  4. Escalation: if not resolved in 10m, page platform oncall lead and IC.
  5. Post-incident: create a postmortem link, tag incident severity, and add corrective actions to backlog.

- Runbook: GPU pool scheduler failures / nodes NotReady
  1. Detect: alert "gpu-pool node NotReady" or scheduling backlog > 5 pending pods for 10m.
  2. Immediate mitigation:
     a. Check node status: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu.
     b. If nodes NotReady due to driver crash: restart node agent: ssh to host -> sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service (on-prem) or cordon node and replace in autoscaling group (cloud provider).
     c. If OOM during model load: identify offending model versions and evict low-priority jobs: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data <node>.
  3. Capacity workaround: scale up burst pool (infra-gpu runbook) to shift non-critical workloads.
  4. Escalate to infra-gpu oncall if manual host intervention required.
  5. Post-incident: snapshot node logs, attach nvml traces, and file a follow-up for root cause and remediation.

4) How-tos (procedures owners will use frequently)
- Adding a new service dashboard (Grafana):
  1. Create a new dashboard folder under dashboard/team/<service-name>.
  2. Start from "Platform service template" and import panels: errors, latency histogram, throughput, resource utilization.
  3. Add alert rules: p50/p95/p99 panels -> alert threshold expressions.
  4. Add dashboard link to service README and notify observability channel for review.
  Example Grafana query (requests per second): sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"service-name\"}[1m])) by (route)

- Oncall handover checklist (start of shift):
  1. Review Platform Overview dashboard for anomalies.
  2. Check open P1/P2 incidents and current pager status.
  3. Read last 24h incident summaries.
  4. Acknowledge any persistent alerts and annotate runbook steps taken.

5) Retrospectives (recent learnings)
- Q2 2026 retrospective highlights:
  - We improved median model load time by 35% after lazy-loading KV caches and adjusting prefetch policies.
  - Alert noise reduced by 42% following threshold tuning and moving to composite alerts for correlated spikes.
  - Capacity planning missed high-concurrency tails for a new customer; action: add workload-specific load test in perf suite.
  Action items:
  - Add a per-customer concurrency simulation to perf-suite (owner: runtime-team, due: 2026-09-01).
  - Create a "canary traffic" automatic rollout step for model variants (owner: platform-api, due: 2026-10-15).

6) Roadmap (next 6–12 months)
- Q3 2026:
  - Unified observability: consolidate dashboard templates and introduce service metadata linking (owner: observability, target: 2026-09-30).
  - Auto-tuning alerts: prototype ML-driven alert threshold suggestions (owner: eng-platform, target: 2026-10-15).
- Q4 2026:
  - Dedicated GPU autoscaler improvements (predictive scaling by workload mix) (owner: infra-gpu, target: 2026-12-15).
  - Runbook automation: add remediation playbooks for common issues (k8s cordon/drain, traffic reroute) via Runbook Runner (owner: platform-ops, target: 2026-12-01).

7) Ownership, cadence, and governance
- Owners must maintain dashboards and runbooks for their services. Oncall rotations: 7-day primary, 14-day secondary.
- Weekly ops review: Tuesday 09:30 UTC — incidents, capacity, and ongoing action items.
- Monthly reliability review: first Monday of month — SLO compliance and retrospective updates.
- Documentation governance: all runbooks must be reviewed quarterly. Changes require a peer reviewer and the oncall lead's signoff.

8) Post-incident workflow and templates
- Postmortem template (use for any P1/P2 incident):
  - Title
  - Severity and timeline
  - Impact summary
  - Root cause
  - Immediate mitigations
  - Long-term fixes and owners
  - Learnings and metrics to track
